overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the January 14 minutes were approved within the timely window, posting online is not required by law, and broader ongoing allegations were not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to timely approve and post the minutes of its January 14 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the January 14 minutes were approved in a timely manner and the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that approved committee minutes had not been published or posted online.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not require that public bodies post their minutes to a website or elsewhere, but only that minutes be approved in a timely manner and made available within 10 days of a request.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the minutes violations were ongoing; the AG limited review to the January 14 minutes and declined broader review.
allegations.key_passage: Complainants must allege violations with a degree of specificity, as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
